title: Startup Launches Humanoid Robot for Under $30,000
key_facts: Feather Robotics Inc., a startup in East Palo Alto, California, has introduced a two-armed wheeled humanoid robot priced under $30,000.
Each arm moves in seven degrees of freedom; each arm is rated to carry 4 pounds, with a peak of 15 pounds.
Arms take human-like hands or parallel-jaw grippers, swappable in the field.
The wheeled base moves in any direction without turning, tops out at 1.3 meters per second, fits through standard doors and weighs 105 kilograms fully configured.
Two hot-swappable 25 amp-hour batteries give 10 hours of operating time.
It has a 10-inch touch screen and a four-microphone array with speaker for conversations.

It is sold as an open platform with an open SDK: customers can run AI models from Nvidia, Skild or Physical Intelligence on it, unlike Figure, Tesla, Unitree, Agibot and 1X, which build body and AI model together.
CEO and co-founder Hoa Mai hopes it becomes the Android of robotics; the article says engineers can go from a trained model to physical deployment in weeks.
quote_evidence: Tech startup Feather Robotics Inc. has introduced a humanoid robot for less than $30,000.
Mai hopes his machine becomes the Android of robotics.
Customers are then free to run models from Nvidia, Skild or Physical Intelligence on it.
why_it_matters_hint: A low-priced robot body without its own AI could let small teams test physical AI without building hardware.
notes: Single trade-magazine report based on company claims; no independent test. Exact price ($29,990) is from the chunk curator note, the article says only 'less than $30,000', so the entry uses the article wording. Pool score 7 set by Rafi's order of 10 Oct 2026 (curator score 5).
